analysis.title: GS Early Morning Research Recap: Ratings and Target Price Changes - November 2, 2026 as of 5:30 AM ET
key_insights: GS leads the day's calls with a US midterm elections preview (Phillips) and an oil forecast raise on high supply disruption risks (Struyven).
GS published November 2026 Conviction List updates for the US (Kron, mid-earnings thoughts), Europe (Graham) and APAC (Snaith).
APAC Conviction List adds Elite Material, Yokohama Rubber and JSW Steel, and removes NYPCB, Shengyi Tech and Hong Kong Exchanges.
Global Technology (Ng) raised its global data center capacity estimates.
Europe Nicotine (Adamski) upgrades British American Tobacco to Buy from Neutral, and Imperial Brands remains a Buy.
APAC Tech (Lee) reads across from Kioxia's CY3Q26 results: mid- to long-term NAND outlook intact, Buy on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
South Korea Tech: October DRAM exports hit a record US$34bn, +595% y/y.
Floor & Decor (FND) is downgraded to Sell from Neutral on moderating 2027 unit growth and a lowered FY26 guide amid macro pressures. Target price is cut to $38 from $53.
Kia is downgraded to Neutral from Buy after a 3Q26 operating profit miss on cost pressures GS expects to persist. Target price is cut to W120,000 from W210,000.
Skshu Paint is downgraded to Sell from Buy after a 3Q26 miss and persistent demand weakness. Target price is cut to Rmb16.90 from Rmb28.40.
Amphenol (APH) stays Buy and is on the regional Conviction List (Buy* from Buy).
Brazil sold off 23% on a surprise election outcome per the GS EM Weekly Kickstart, and MSCI EM fell 1% w/w.
GS Asia-Pacific and Taiwan Kickstarts note renewed Tech/AI stress late in the week, continued foreign selling and 3Q26 earnings that have broadly missed expectations, especially on margins.
The GS BoE preview expects a hike with noncommittal guidance, and the Japan flash expects the BOJ on hold now with the next hike forecast for December.
GS October GSAI note is titled 'All Tricks, No Treats' and the G10 Consumer Dashboard shows a US and UK slowdown with improvement in the Euro Area and Canada.

Earnings recaps in the list include beats at Veralto, Colgate, Church & Dwight, Crocs, Mondelez, Capri (FY27 raise), Regeneron, Gilead, Insmed and Digital Realty, plus misses or cuts at Hershey (FY27 cost pressure), Coinbase (weaker near-term revenue outlook), Intel (PC weakness) and Haleon (guidance cut on China and LatAm).
Alstom issued profit warnings for FY26/27 and Ryanair reported broadly in line FQ2 results with a new buyback from Feb-27.
GS commentary on Amazon, Reddit and Roblox 3Q26 reviews, and a Sandisk note on tight supply/demand with rising datacenter exposure.

sector_views.rationale: BAT upgraded to Buy and Imperial remains a Buy as growth meets value.
Mid- to long-term NAND outlook intact after Kioxia read-across, Buy on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
Floor & Decor downgraded to Sell on moderating 2027 unit growth and macro pressure.

earnings_insights: Floor & Decor lowered FY26 guidance and now sees moderating 2027 unit growth, per the downgrade to Sell.
Kia 3Q26 operating profit missed on cost pressures GS expects to persist.
Skshu Paint 3Q26 missed on persistent demand weakness.
Veralto 3Q26 beat with FY2026 outlook raised and growth accelerating into 4Q (reported 10/30-31).
Capri F2Q27 beat with an FY27 raise, focus on Michael Kors recovery.
Crocs reported a strong 3Q26 beat with a guidance raise.
Colgate-Palmolive reported a Q3 beat and raised FY26 guidance. Church & Dwight reported a Q3 beat and raised FY26 topline guidance.
Mondelez reported a 3Q beat and reiterated FY26 guidance. Hershey said incremental cost pressures weigh on its FY27 outlook.
Kenvue reported in-line Q3 EPS as stronger organic sales growth and gross margins were partly offset by higher SG&A.
Haleon cut guidance on unexpected China and LatAm headwinds, with EPS cut by 3% (reported 10/29).
Coinbase showed expense discipline and growth in newer products but a weaker near-term revenue outlook.

TFI International 3Q26 EPS missed on weaker less-than-truckload profits. Canadian National 3Q26 EPS beat with FY26 EPS growth guide kept at mid- to high-single digit versus about high-single-digit consensus.
Alstom issued profit warnings for FY26/27 (reported 11/2).
Intel: servers very strong but PC weakness likely to be a setback for the stock.
Kioxia 2Q in line, with 3Q guidance below expectations partly on a shipment timing shift.
CXMT 3Q26 gross margin up to 90% with a 3Q26 beat.
Norwegian Cruise Line 3Q26 review: greenshoots emerge, 2027 yield growth still a show-me story. Hilton Grand Vacations lowered guidance, weighing on long-term estimates.

macro_indicators.indicator: South Korea Kia October global wholesale
macro_indicators.interpretation: Kia wholesale grew despite the 3Q26 operating profit miss and downgrade.
Global revenue passenger kilometers declined in September.

macro_indicators.indicator: UK household appliance and consumer (HAC) growth
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS sees minimal near-term budget impact on UK HAC while shifting growth from 2027 to 2026.
GS expects the BoE to hike without committing to further moves.
BOJ held as expected on 10/30, and GS now forecasts the next hike in December.
Two-wheeler retail grew while car retail fell.

crypto_views: Coinbase (COIN) shows robust expense discipline and growth in newer products, offset by a weaker near-term revenue outlook, per GS.
risk_factors: Renewed Tech/AI stress late in the week drove foreign outflows across Asia.
3Q26 earnings in Asia-Pacific, Taiwan and North Asia/China have broadly missed expectations, mainly on margins.
Macro pressure on home-related consumer spending (Floor & Decor guidance cut).
Cost pressures weigh on Kia and Hershey outlooks.
Weaker PC demand is a risk for Intel.
Brazil election surprise and its market impact.
Opening of an Agios sickle cell PDUFA delay on potential REMS inclusion.
vol_and_positioning: EM saw heavy foreign selling in October led by North Asia, and EM and Asia mutual funds fell around 8-9% in October.
Taiwan retail continued to add exposure via ETFs and leverage while foreigners sold, and TAIEX fell another 2%.
India outperformed in October amid an anti-AI rotation, with foreign inflows intensifying, and NIFTY rebounded +2% in the week.
KOSPI rebounded 3% in the week despite the Wall Street tech sell-off.
A-shares fell 3% on further global tech weakness while H-shares were flat, and Southbound ETF Connect was expanded.
geopolitical: Brazil surprise election outcome drove a 23% sell-off in Brazilian equities, with GS hosting a Brazil post-election call.
US midterm elections previewed by GS Economics, with webinars scheduled November 4-5.
Oil forecast raised on high supply disruption risks.
UK budget (Worry-free budget per GS UK Kickstart) had minimal near-term impact on retail HAC.
Section 232 tariffs referenced as a benefit to First Solar with more clarity into 2027.
